sections.text: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix after a race defined by 34 lead changes. The event involved constant battling between Red Bull, Mercedes, and McLaren. George Russell crashed late in the race, while Kimi Antonelli lost positions to Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri on the final lap. Ferrari drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton both received 10-second penalties for driving infringements.

sections.text: The race was described as reminiscent of American oval racing, differing significantly from typical Formula 1 events. It highlighted the impact of the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines on competitive dynamics. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq, pricing its IPO at $83 a share before it rose to $111. The lab behind Claude became one of the most valuable companies on the planet amid peak AI hype. Competitors like OpenAI reportedly let Anthropic go public first to test market reactions and observe how investors value competitor revenue.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Anthropic must balance its commitment to AI safety branding with the profit-oriented demands of the public markets and increasing compute bills totalling roughly $900 billion. Its business model relies heavily on convincing enterprise and government customers to pay for safe, trustworthy AI despite increasing price sensitivity and cheaper open-source alternatives.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The upcoming quarters will reveal whether Anthropic can drive the massive revenue growth needed to deliver a return to investors. Analysts estimate significant revenue increases will be required to fund new models while maintaining expensive safety efforts under complex governance.

sections.text: Reports indicate that both the FBI and the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) were hacked. This issue has caused the couple to stop kissing and has negatively affected their physical intimacy.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Former Prime Minister Theresa May criticised Prime Minister Andy Burnham for considering further negotiations regarding the European Union, insisting Brexit is finished. Her comments followed Burnham securing a deal with the EU covering food exports, emissions trading, and a youth scheme. Meanwhile, former Prime Minister Sir Tony Blair stated the UK should only rejoin the bloc if it reforms its technology policies.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: May warned that reopening EU negotiations consumes excessive government time and distracts from pressing economic and security priorities. However, Burnham described his recent Brussels agreement as mutually beneficial, while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen highlighted the joint potential for technological innovation.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Burnham announced that both sides will hold an informal brainstorming process to explore future relationship options prior to the upcoming UK-EU summit. He did not state that rejoining the EU would be discussed.

sections.text: A fire broke out at a confectionery factory in Serang district, Banten province, on Saturday. gist: Data centers and generative AI have become political flashpoints due to massive resource demands.
Communities globally are pushing back against the physical presence and environmental impacts of data centers.
Tech companies are responding with public relations shifts, though critics remain sceptical about true benefits.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Journalist Paris Marx investigated the impact of data centers and generative AI in a new book titled Hyperscale. Data center backlash has emerged as a motivating factor in midterm elections and a unifying political issue across communities facing pressures on electricity and water resources.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The rapid buildout of hyperscale facilities creates severe environmental and social costs, including increased fossil fuel energy demand and water scarcity in stressed regions. Communities feel these material impacts directly through noise, power bills, and resource strain, driving widespread opposition to big tech infrastructure.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Major tech companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI have pledged to stop using non-disclosure agreements in local government negotiations and are proposing infrastructure and cooling alternatives. However, opposition is expected to continue as long as communities shoulder the heavy resource costs without seeing tangible public benefits.

The center manages International Space Station operations and prepares crews for deep space.
Johnson teams are developing capabilities for sustained human presence on the Moon.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston has led American human spaceflight for 65 years. Established as the Manned Spacecraft Center in November 1961, it managed the Gemini, Apollo, Skylab and Space Shuttle programs. Its Mission Control Center became operational in June 1965 during Gemini IV. Johnson has also overseen management of the International Space Station, which has sustained continuous human habitation for over 26 years.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The center has developed critical spaceflight techniques, including rendezvous, docking and spacewalks. It curates Apollo lunar samples, supports astronaut training, conducts microgravity health research and manages international partner operations for space station missions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Johnson teams are preparing for future lunar exploration under the Artemis and Moon Base programs. Following Artemis II and III tests, Artemis IV aims to land astronauts on the Moon, while phased plans prepare for long-term presence near the lunar South Pole.

gist: An Oxfam report states Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into a toxic wasteland.
Contamination from debris, sewage and munitions poses long-term health risks to Palestinians.
Oxfam calls for an independent environmental assessment to identify risks before reconstruction.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An Oxfam report states Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into a toxic wasteland, with 99% of the territory showing contamination indicators. Debris, heavy metals, explosive residues and sewage pollute the environment. Israel maintains its military campaign is self-defence against Hamas and has rejected genocide allegations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Contamination poses severe chronic health risks for Gazans, including respiratory diseases, cancers, birth defects and skin conditions. Untreated sewage is contaminating groundwater and the sea, preventing safe food production.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Oxfam calls for a detailed independent environmental assessment before reconstruction begins. However, Israel has conditioned large-scale reconstruction in Gaza on the complete disarmament of Hamas and other armed groups.

quotes.text: There are going to be chronic health impacts that are long term because a lot of these contaminants are persistent in the environment,

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Illegal artisanal gold mining has increased in Madagascar, driven by record high gold prices and failing crops caused by climate change. In the Mangabe reserve, miners have dug numerous holes in marshy ground, destroying the habitats of the endangered golden mantella frog.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Madagascar is a major biodiversity hotspot, but widespread poverty leaves many residents living on very little per day. Communities turn to illegal mining for quick money, while authorities lack the resources to regulate the sector properly, leading to severe deforestation and population declines in endemic wildlife.

sections.text: A scruffy stray dog was spotted at a construction site on the Baltimore-Washington Parkway in March. Workers built her a small shack, but she ran off when they got too close. She was underweight, covered in ticks, and enduring night temperatures around -10C.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The dog survived harsh winter conditions on her own for several months. Despite her ordeal, she quickly settled into a loving home, showing a unique personality and a deep love for exploration.

sections.heading: What happens next

articles.title: Arctic air brings colder temperatures to Europe this week
articles.standfirst: After a warmer-than-average November so far globally, a cold snap is on the horizon in parts of Europe

timeline.text: Arctic air brings colder temperatures to Europe this week

gist: Arctic air is sweeping across Europe, bringing plunging temperatures and widespread snowfall this week.
Temperatures in parts of Europe will fall below zero, contrasting with ongoing global record warmth.
Ski resorts in the Alps could receive a significant boost of snow from the low pressure.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Arctic air swept across a large swathe of Europe, opening a corridor of cold air driven by high pressure over Scandinavia and low pressure shifting into western Russia. Temperatures in countries such as Germany, Poland, Ukraine, and the Baltics fell widely below zero, with ice days anticipated. Extensive snowfall also occurred in regions including southern Poland, Belarus, Ukraine, and the Alps.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The cold spell in Europe contrasts starkly with global temperature trends, which continue to set records through a strong El Niño. Meanwhile, the significant dumping of snow provides a welcome boost for ski resorts in the Alps ahead of their upcoming openings.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: High pressure is set to remain dominant across northern Europe into the weekend and early December, maintaining below-average temperatures in central and eastern Europe and potentially extending into the Balkans. Cold easterly winds might also reach western Europe and the UK.

Americans criticised the Trump administration and contractor L3Harris over infrastructure failures.
Citizens raised concerns regarding competence, accountability, and the impact of federal layoffs.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all US flights following a data overload caused by a router installation by contractor L3Harris. Separate outages also affected Microsoft services, leading to widespread disruption.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Americans expressed deep distrust and outrage over the outages. Critics blamed government layoffs, contractor relationships, and a lack of backup systems for making the nation's critical infrastructure vulnerable.

A router installation caused a data overload in telecommunications infrastructure, exposing a lack of backup systems and federal competency.

gist: A report revealed unnecessary and intimidating force was used against asylum seekers removed from the UK.
Deportation flights under the one in, one out scheme involved vulnerable people and restraint incidents.
Inspectors found issues including poor leadership, ineffective interpretation tools, and degrading treatment.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A report examined deportation charter flights under the UK and France scheme, identifying use-of-force incidents. Inspectors reviewed body-worn footage showing vulnerable individuals subjected to waist restraint belts and leg restraints, poor carrying techniques, and degrading conditions such as being given bags to urinate into during van transport.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Many of those deported fled conflict zones and survived torture or trafficking. articles.title: Presidential villa suffers water and power cuts, Nigerian leader says
articles.standfirst: Bola Tinubu says he was shaving last week when the water cut out - an experience familiar to many Nigerians.

timeline.text: Presidential villa suffers water and power cuts, Nigerian leader says

gist: Nigeria's president stated that the presidential villa experienced water and power cuts.
The Nigerian leader experienced a water outage while shaving at Aso Rock last week.
Nigeria faces widespread electricity and water shortages affecting households and businesses.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Nigeria's president revealed that the presidential villa in Abuja suffered from interruptions to both its water and electricity supplies. The leader recounted that the water stopped running while he was shaving last week.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlights infrastructure problems that are common for ordinary citizens across the nation. Nigeria experiences frequent electricity disruptions driven by gas shortages and low hydropower output, alongside chronic water shortages caused by rapid population growth and decaying public infrastructure.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The president has vowed to correct these issues and improve conditions. Supporters note recent rural electricity improvements and a newly approved investment in a transmission grid expansion to address the ongoing power crisis ahead of future political contests.

fivew: The presidential residence experienced unexpected water and electricity cuts.
At Aso Rock in Abuja, Nigeria.
To highlight infrastructure challenges and promise improvements.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Doctors in Northern Ireland began a strike involving Christmas Day cover, affecting hospital appointments, routine investigations and routine operating lists. The health minister stated the strike would impact around 1,694 patients.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Striking doctors expressed feeling aggrieved over pay compared to colleagues across the UK and cited concerns about delivering care in difficult conditions. sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Rescheduled appointments and procedures will be rearranged as soon as possible, while further consequences for patients are anticipated heading into the winter period due to the knock-on effects of rescheduled activity.

gist: Manchester United's managerial hiring and firing costs approach £100m since 2013.
The club borrowed £10m shortly after confirming Mauricio Pochettino as head coach.
Michael Carrick was sacked with the club in the relegation zone.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester United appointed Mauricio Pochettino on a two-and-a-half-year deal and will pay £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer. The club borrowed £10m three days later. Michael Carrick was sacked as manager last week after the club entered the relegation zone.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The latest compensation package pushes the total spent on hiring and firing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired to £95m, with costs expected to exceed £100m. United's overall revolving credit debt reached £240m, alongside outstanding transfer fees of £417m.

articles.standfirst: Nine days after playing for Greece in a nightmare 7-0 loss, keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis plays a pivotal role in Hull's Premier League win against Brighton.

timeline.text: From conceding seven to Hull heroics - how Tzolakis recovered to defy Brighton

gist: Hull goalkeeper Tzolakis made crucial saves to prevent Brighton from scoring on Sunday.
Brighton missed the opportunity to move within three points of leaders Arsenal.
Pundits praised Tzolakis for his dominant and decisive goalkeeping performance.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Hull goalkeeper Tzolakis produced an outstanding defensive display to deny Brighton a victory on Sunday. The former Olympiacos shot-stopper, signed in August for a reported £20m, made key saves against Diego Gomez, Georginio Rutter, Pascal Gross and Lewis Dunk. Brighton also hit the crossbar through Yasin Ayari, while Regan Slater cleared a shot from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line after Tzolakis slowed it down.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The draw prevented Brighton from closing the gap on league leaders Arsenal to three points. For Hull, Tzolakis demonstrated his value following his summer transfer, earning high praise from pundits Clinton Morrison and Danny Murphy for his commanding performance.

quotes.text: We saw again how important Tzolakis is for Hull.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Mauricio Pochettino's reign as Manchester United head coach began with a 4-0 defeat by Liverpool at Anfield. Defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Pochettino insisted his team made an unbelievable effort, whereas former captain Roy Keane called the performance rubbish. Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola considered the red card justified.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The result leaves Manchester United 19th in the Premier League table after 11 games, 20 points behind Arsenal. It equals the joint-worst debut result for any Manchester United manager.

gist: Australia defeated Wales in a close Nations Championship match in Cardiff.
Wales fought back with tries from Dewi Lake and Blair Murray.
Australia held on despite a late yellow card to secure victory.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Australia edged past Wales in a tight contest at the Principality Stadium. Tries from Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau helped the visitors build a lead. Wales responded through captain Dewi Lake who scored twice, alongside a try from Blair Murray, but Australia ultimately held on for the win.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory ended a four-match losing run for Australia and secured the Nations Championship spoils. For Wales, the defeat highlighted missed attacking opportunities after they failed to capitalise on their chances following their previous notable win against New Zealand.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Wales will play Japan at Twickenham on Saturday. Australia are scheduled to face Ireland on Friday.

gist: England beat New Zealand 37-12 in a repeat of last year.
England played with a more fluid and less predictable style.
New Zealand struggled after a long and tiring schedule.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England secured a 37-12 victory over New Zealand in front of 81,953 fans. Unlike last year when they relied heavily on kicking, England played a more fluid passing game and scored tries through clever movement. Ben Earl made 33 carries, while the forward pack and defence dominated the match against a depleted visiting side.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Steve Borthwick's team has experienced many false dawns and fluctuating form over four years. This win suggests England may have developed a more sustainable tactical approach and deeper squad balance to challenge rugby superpowers ahead of next year's World Cup.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: New Zealand will face England again next Saturday at Allianz Stadium in the Nations Championship third-place play-off. Meanwhile, England's next major challenge will be an away match against Ireland in the Six Nations tournament next February.

Shevchenko lying about drugs test claims - Mudryk

gist: Andriy Shevchenko accused Mykhailo Mudryk's camp of seeking a false scapegoat for a doping test.
Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed test and subsequent 20-month ban.
Shevchenko denied the allegations, defending the association and asking Mudryk to retract his comments.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Andriy Shevchenko stated that Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives repeatedly asked for a football federation employee to falsely take the blame for Mudryk's positive test for meldonium. Mudryk, suspended from November 2024 to July 2026, blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for the failed test, claiming it happened on international duty and criticizing a lack of support.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Shevchenko called the claims baseless slander and defended the professionalism of association staff, while Mudryk argued the handling of the matter delayed his return to football.

fivew: Andriy Shevchenko accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of asking an employee to falsely take the blame for a positive drugs test.
Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed drugs test, prompting a public response from Shevchenko.

quotes.text: baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally
